D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black) I wanted an ILM camera I could use with low f-stop manual lenses. I have some nice old f/1.9 & f/2.8 MC Rokkor lenses from 45 years ago.
My Lumix ZS70 is great for everything but low light & a few specialized uses. For those you need interchangeable lenses.
This package with two kit lenses is roughly the equivalent of my ZS70. Both lenses work fine. I'm still learning the menus & controls. It handles well on my monopod.
Edit:
I bought an inexpensive Fotasy adapter for the Minolta lenses. It works fine. The camera switches to full manual mode automatically. I did take some online advice & set up two of the programmable buttons for peaking & magnification to help with manual focusing. The resulting shutter speeds are nice, up to 8 times faster.
Edit:
This is a small camera, only a little larger than a P&S. That's normally good. Except when the temperatures are in the teens (F). Even thin leather driving gloves are a bit clumsy, especially with the back panel buttons. I normally use fingerless mittens, but not this morning.
Edit:
I'm really liking this camera. My lens changing/handling skills are coming back after not being used for [cough] years. In terms of focal lengths, the basic kit lens (14-42mm) is good for 80% of shots. I'd wish for a couple of more f-stops, though.
Edit, 5/16/2020
Longer term: Still good. I have the F3 button set on MF. There are a few cases where the AF algorithm & I disagree. For some reason, buttercup yellow flowers have no inherent contrast & AF has a hard time seeing the details to focus. This brings up peaking & magnify & allows me to fine tune the focus.
I keep wishing for a 20-80 mm f/2.8 lens. Cheap, of course. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black)

Skullcandy Crusher ANC Personalized Noise Canceling Wireless Headphone - Black Hands down the best headphones I've ever put on for bass. I ran them through my audio tester and these picked up way lower tones than my Senn's which have been my long standing pair for bass. It does seem to come at that cost of picking up the higher notes, but honestly when pitches are that high, they are annoying and I'm fine with the headphones not picking them up. I don't need to hear a dog whistle...

Mid-range was true, sound was immersive, the headset was light and comfortable. A bit warm on the ears but pretty much all closed style headsets are.
So why the three stars?
OMG the constant never ending hissing. Unless you are playing something loud enough to cover it up, it is always there. Even when I turned off ANC, even when I switched to ambient mode. HIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSS. I tried to ignore it but it was always there. I work on the computer and sometimes I have to hear audio tracks and othertimes there is silence, I have to physically remove these every time I am not playing something or HIIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSSS. Honestly have no idea how other reviews aren't bothered by this, its the loudest hissing static I've ever heard coming through headsets.

If you are like me and do not have sound coming out the entire time you are wearing them, do not buy. They will make you insane with rage, RAAWWRRR.

If you are only going to wear them while listening to music, and want the best bass you can find, buy these they are AMAZING for that, seriously. But ugh that hissing.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Crusher ANC Personalized Noise Canceling Wireless Headphone - Black

ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This timer is a good size with a very readable LED display and a strong magnet on the clip on the back to hold it to your fridge or whatever a magnet will stick to. The buttons are large and accessible, and it's really no problem to set it up. It beeps loudly when the time is up, so there's little danger you're not going to hear it from an adjoining room.

Strangely, on day one (unlike with some timers I've used), the first three or four times that I held down the hour, minute, or second buttons to speed up the counting and turn off the beeps, it just froze and stopped counting. If I pressed the button over and over to advance the counter by one, it worked—beeping annoyingly loudly each time, of course. I was about to give it a two-star review and throw it away because I couldn't stand it, but I put off doing it and just stuck it to the top of my stove. A week later, after I'd used the stove several times and the timer probably got exposed to some heat, I went back to try it again so I could write this review and the fast-count sans beeps feature worked. Weird. Maybe it was just stressed in shipping and needed time to settle down....

A few things I really do dislike is that it's easy to reset the time by mistake if the grey button on the left gets slid up; the modes are manually set with this button. (That approach to the modes could be good for the technologically challenged, though.) Also, if you overshoot your mark on the time, there is no way to go backward; you have to go forward until you come back around to where you were supposed to have stopped the first time. The clip is a little too sharply angled, so when you stick the timer to a surface with the magnet, the face slants down somewhat, but it's still visible; really not that big of a deal.

Another thing, as I've remarked about another MeasuPro product: the how-to info on the packaging is white letters on light grey, which is practically unreadable for anyone, not just people like me with old eyes. (The company told me they were correcting that with the other product, so I expect they will do the same with this one.)
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

text_fidelity_a:
Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite While this flash doesn’t outperform the Canon Speedlite, it comes the closest of any of the Speedlite “clones” I’ve tried so far, and does so with impressive build quality.

I was impressed with this right out of the box mainly due to the care taken with packaging. No, packaging doesn’t impact the performance of the flash, but it does take the worry out of getting one that is damaged due to UPS handling. The flash is packed in a carry case (which is very well-made and has cushioning) and, in turn, packed inside of an air-filled tube case. Together they provide more than ample protection against transit-born bruises short of being run over by the UPS truck.

The flash feels very solid. The head articulates up/down/left/right and has indents at the most commonly used angles. The head is a bit stiff to move, but I consider that as a positive since I don’t want the head getting bumped out of place when I have it positioned the way I want it.

The hotshoe frame is plastic but feels very solid. There’s a rotating locking ring to keep it in place while on the camera. It made contact and worked just fine on a 5D Mark II, a 4D and a Rebel.

The battery compartment door has a spring-loaded hinge so it pops up when unlatched. Again, good build quality on that (which is a common point of failure on other low-cost flashes I’ve used). It uses 4 AA batteries. It ran fine on rechargeables.

The control panel and LCD screen are both easy to use and see for the most part. The buttons beep when pressed, but that can be turned off if you want a silent operation. Some of the icons on the screen are very small – I needed to squint a bit to make some of them out. Then again, my aging eyes could be a contributing factor.

Most of the commands are executed by pressing a button and then selecting options using a rotating wheel. The wheel is the only part that didn’t work all that well at times. Sometimes a single twist moved it through the menu; other times I needed to twist it a couple of times to get it to register.

The capabilities of this flash are very impressive given the price point. It offers synch flash, manual flash, curtain synch, up to 1/8000 second synch, master/slave mode, AF assist beam, TTL flash, zoom settings and an LED lamp. It also has a nice amount of convenience features such as auto off (with various timed settings ranging from 5 minutes to 2 hours), a lock mode, screen on/off and test mode. It even has a USB port that can be used to update the firmware should updates be available (at this writing I am not aware of any updates).

The manual is not great. It offers a decent listing of the capabilities, but is often sparse in pointing out the details. But, if you have some measure of experience with a flash, it’s not hard to figure out (with a bit of experimenting) how to use it.

Given the price, this is an excellent value. It probably won’t suit the needs of a professional photographer but for an amateur (even a very avid one) it’s an excellent alternative to Canon gear at a much nicer price.
text_fidelity_b: Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite

text_fidelity_a:
WiFi Extender Long Range Repeater 300Mbps Router Wireless Access Point Signal Amplifier Booster Complies with 802.11n/g/b with WPS Button,Extends WiFi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices Just got this today because we are having wifi accessibility issues in our upstairs guest bedroom (and every good host knows that if you don't have decent wifi in your guest room, you can expect your guests to leave you a holy mess, in retaliation).

Couldn't believe how easy this is to set up, though! I'm pretty tech-savvy, anyhow (after 2 years of various tech-related military schools). Not that I needed to be! The included instructions are incredibly clear and easy to follow. On the contrary, the last AP/repeater I bought merely schooled me in when it's acceptable to take a hammer to one of these things. (FYI: it's right after you've tried, unsuccessfully, for an hour to get it to connect to your wifi). So I really appreciated how simple and fast this is to set up.

How fast, exactly? It literally took like 2 minutes to set up...and only THAT long because I had to go all the way into the other room and log into my laptop to complete the instructions.

Just a head's up, for the less-tech savvy:

This is NOT a wifi signal amplifier, as such. You WILL be creating a NEW wireless access point (aka wifi log-on)...even if you install this in "repeater" mode--vs. the wired-to-wireless AP (access point) mode.

So, for example, instead of logging into whatever your network is called, when you need to use the wifi that this repeats for you, you'll be logging into a new connection. They call it, by default, "My Repeater" (I assume that is so you'll never forget who actually owns it), but you can rename it to anything you want (mine is henceforth known as Fluffy Gigglebuns). You'll still use the same password as you use for your main connection, though...and therein lies the genius of it. You can make your guests feel special (or, in my case, humiliated) by personalizing the repeater network name, but the password will be the same as it is for whatever network AP you are having it repeat.

Lastly, this does offer an extra feature I think is worth mentioning:

You can also use this as a wireless adapter to connect a multimedia or other tech device that requires or ONLY allows internet connectivity via an ethernet (aka wired) connection.

So if you have something like an older roku, or game console, etc. that can only connect to the internet via an ethernet cable, you can apparently use THIS device to quickly convert it to use your wifi connection.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Extender Long Range Repeater 300Mbps Router Wireless Access Point Signal Amplifier Booster Complies with 802.11n/g/b with WPS Button,Extends WiFi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Philips CAM150BU/37 Waterproof 8 MP Digital Camera with CMOS Sensor and 4 x Optical Zoom (Black) I have to say, I was excited to get this thanks to the zoom for the video, but I was sorely disappointed in its quality. The indoor video I took of my son's music concert, in admittedly relatively low-light (but nowhere near dark) was nearly unwatchable. The focus was terrible and the output was super grainy. My wife, sitting right next to me and thus experiencing the exact same environment, taped the show using our Kodak playsport and it came out absolutely wonderful, well worth sending out to family members. There was simply no comparison between the two. While the sound quality was a closer match, I'd still give the nod to the Kodak over the Phillips. The still photos in the same situation came out just as bad, also grainy, also often blurry, and often washed-out as well. I tried both video and stills at various levels of zoom--without a zoom the quality of both was noticeably better, but still poor quality. I then took stills out in a well-lit hallway and again was disappointed in the quality and again, the Kodak completely outmatched the Phillips.

I've used it in outdoor conditions and better lit conditions and there's no doubt the picture quality is better in those conditions, but in all of them it comes in quite below the Kodak in quality.

Other issues:

The zoom was very slow to auto-focus and took several long seconds before settling in.

the choice of a micro-SD. Not only is it annoyingly different, which I could live with, but it really took some force to get it into the slot. In fact, the first time I used it I left it sticking partway out assuming it was a clever design that shutting the cover would put the card into the slot as it needed to go. This did work--the card obviously slipped in and had no issues--but then, when I needed to connect it to the computer to download, which necessitates leaving the cover open for the cable, I realized what I had thought was a clever design wasn't purposeful, as I needed to get the card all the way in. I eventually used a pen cap to push it in, wincing at the pressure needed to do so. (I won't discuss the times it popped out and I had to search on the floor/desk for it).

it has its pluses, but to be honest, since its primary purpose is taking good pictures and video, and so far it hasn't, I don't see the point in outlining the good points which are so secondary to its primary objective.

I'll use it a few more times to ensure this review is a fair one, but there is no way I will do so at special events or without using the Kodak as backup (or one of my point-and-shoots which also shoot far better video based on the samples so far--two Canon elphs and our larger Canon IS). At this point, not only would I not use this but I wouldn't give it to a friend. But as mentioned, I'll give it a few more chances and report back.
text_fidelity_b: Philips CAM150BU/37 Waterproof 8 MP Digital Camera with CMOS Sensor and 4 x Optical Zoom (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I'm a big fan of Kindle e-Readers. We own two of the older generation ones (the last Kindles with keyboard) and for x-mas I bought my mother a Kindle Fire HD 8.9 for x-mas. But, alas, she doesn't seem to have fine enough motor control to hit the small buttons on that device (see my review for that device). So the Fire has been sitting unused on the coffee table for a few months now.

But this is not a review of the Fire HD 8.9. I want to describe my very short experience with the basic Kindle and the Kindle Paperwhite - as they relate to the intended user: my mom. She recently suffered a stroke and one of the side effects is that she now has a constant tremble in her left hand. As she had trouble with the Fire HD 8.9 we went to Staples to see if the more purpose-built Kindles were easier to operate. We were not surprised when she often made mistakes selecting books on the Paperwhite's touch screen. But we were surprised to find that she couldn't even handle the physical buttons on the basic Kindle! From what I could tell, the problems were: the side-buttons (page forward/backward) are much smaller and narrower than they were on our old Kindles (which my mom had no trouble with), so basic navigation among pages became iffy. Similarly, the D-pad is smaller too - and that made selection of books difficult for her. Finally, while I could easily hold my old Kindle with one hand AND operate the page forward button, this is a bit more difficult with the new basic Kindle. My mom could not manage it at all. And since she can't hold the Kindle with her trembling left hand, neither e-Reader was for her. [She is now making do with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 by laying it on a flat surface and only operating it with her right hand].

I'm still giving the Kindle 4 stars because none of these shortcomings are of interest to the majority of people, but I wanted folks to be aware of the newer devices' potential limitations with those suffering from limited motor skills.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire 1 A115-31-C2Y3, 15.6" Full HD Display, Intel Celeron N4020, 4GB DDR4, 64GB eMMC, 802.11ac Wi-Fi 5, Up to 10-Hours of Battery Life, Microsoft 365 Personal, Windows 10 in S mode, Black As far as I can tell, this laptop functions as intended, but I'm finding using it to be a moderately unpleasant experience. At this price, it's not unexpected, but I'm having trouble figuring out an optimal use for it.

The version of Windows (S mode) it uses, won't install most software. You can only install from the Windows store. The best use I can think of for this is that my dad is too old to learn new tricks and could really use a new laptop that functions better than his ancient one, and can't install malware.

The problem is, people who aren't good with computers generally just want to buy a cheap one because they figure they won't use it much. It's self fulfilling. They aren't generally a pleasure to use. In this case, it doesn't have a touchscreen. These days, anyone who isn't between the age of 30 and 50 is probably pushing on their screen when you tell them to click something.

It includes a full tenkey on the keyboard. I would usually like that. Maybe they just had extra space and figured why not? I can't think of who would need the feature. Everyone I can think of who would want a tenkey would be dealing with either gaming or spreadsheets, and would have a nicer machine. At this point I'm thinking maybe a business that wants to cheaply equip a bunch of employees with something they can't screw with in a way that will be problematic. I think it would work fine for that, so long as there is no non-app software that needs to be installed.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers This is by far the best ereader on the market.

The bad.

It doesn't do epub and it doesn't connect to the library. This seems like a deal breaker until you try to borrow a book from the library. I have one on hold now (to read on either the nook or the Sony) that should be available in 39 weeks. I'll probably give up and just buy it anyway.

The good.

The speed. The page turns are as fast as the average person can turn a print page. You won't see that "opening book" message the nook displays. When you tell it to open a book, it opens in less than a second. I keep hitting the page turn key just to marvel at how fast it is. I've never seen an ereader this fast. This is perfect.

Store access. Let me run you through buying a book for the various devices. For the Kindle, if you're on the Amazon site you select your book, click buy now, pick up the device and start reading. For the nook, you buy the book, then you turn on the touch screen that keeps turning itself off, you go into the home screen, go to "My Library", select "Update B&N Content" and wait a few minutes. There is no mechanism to automatically push content to the device. For the Sony (I'm using the Daily Edition, which has 3G), you use the custom software (no way to buy from a website), buy the book, then either transfer it via USB, or go to the device, to the store, log into your account (you need to provide your login information each time you go to the store) find the book you bought and click download, then wait. For buying from the device, Kindle is easy and fast, nook is decent, and Sony is unreasonably slow.

The screen. There is no glare, even with the book light on. It's the crispest and easiest to read screen out there. It's beautiful.

Audible integration. Download your books via WiFi or transfer via USB and listen with your device, either through headphones or the speakers. How cool is that? Now if only there were a card reader to store those larger files.

Collections. I have the Kindle 1, so I was first introduced to collections via Sony. It's great to be able to organize so much content. Here you can organize ebooks and audiobooks into collections together. That's one thing Kindle and Sony both have over nook--they treat content the same. Nook is the only one that doesn't let you annotate or bookmark newspapers and magazines, and who wouldn't want to mark an article to refer back to later?

Ease of use. I handed my Kindle 1 to a woman who was too scared of technology to turn on her own laptop. Her husband had to do it for her. I wanted to show her a passage in the Declaration of Independence, and I had the passage on the screen. I didn't instruct her. Moments later, she turned the page and just kept reading, all the way the end. Then she looked at what else I had on the device. An ereader should be as easy and intuitive to use as a print book, and most of us figured those out when we were about 10 months old. Kindle fits that bill.

Social networking. Post passages and comments on them to Twitter and Facebook. You can see what passages other readers have highlighted. This is particularly great for online book clubs.

More language sets. I'm kind of hoping Amazon will sell Japanese language books in the US Kindle store, or let us buy from Amazon.co.jp.

I could go on and on, but what it comes down to is, when it comes down to the core features of an ereader--buying, reading, annotating, and searching a book, Kindle beats the competition hands down. When it comes to extra bells and whistles--organization, commenting to others, web access, text to speech, Kindle beats the competition hands down.

There is no other viable choice any more. Kindle is just too much better than every other device out there.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation This is a great streaming box! Like the title says, it's a ROKU on steroids. I have an Apple Airport Extreme router and the ROKU would "occasionally" start buffering because of the processor; however, with the Amazon Fire TV, that's not an issue because it has a quad-core processor. Great streaming box!

Updated 5-4-14 I've had the Fire TV for a couple of months now and for the most part it's great; however, today we rented "Bad Grandpa" on Amazon. It played great but when there was 35 mins left in the movie, it quit playing. Tried to restart the movie and got a message saying there was a problem with playing the movie and to contact Amazon Customer Service. I called them and they said that when this happens, "...unplug the Fire TV for 15 seconds and then plug it back in." In my opinion, that takes the fun out of watching a movie! I thought the memory and quad-core processor would be enough to stop this from happening, wrong! Having said that, instead of naming my review "ROKU on Steroids" I should have named it "Just like ROKU".

The Amazon rep said that it was a problem with the memory of the Amazon Fire TV and not the video. When asked if the problem could be fixed by Amazon with an update, all he said was "I'll forward that to Amazon".

If you don't mind watching videos that stop playing and having to unplug the Fire TV and restart it during a movie, you'll really like the Fire TV.

One other point, the Amazon rep stated that it might be my router. I have an Apple Airport Extreme, the best and fastest available. If it was my router, I guess the Amazon rep should have had me unplug my router instead of the Fire TV. He finally admitted that it was the Fire TV and not the router.

Just wanted to get this information out there so people can be informed about the Amazon Fire TV before purchasing one. All in all, I'm happy with the Fire TV...just aggravated that I have to unplug it and restart it when watching movies. The Amazon Fire TV should be better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Lifeproof FRĒ SERIES iPhone 6/6s Waterproof Case (4.7" Version) - Retail Packaging - SUNSET (PIPELINE/WINDSURF/LONGBOARD) I got my mother the Lifeproof FRE case for her iPhone 6. For the last year, she’s been using a cheap case I bought on Amazon, the Diztronic Voyeur Case. I didn’t feel it was protective enough, so I hoped the Lifeproof FRE would work for her.

Unfortunately, she didn’t like the case at all, and wanted it off her phone minutes after I put it on. I made her use it for a few weeks, and while she didn’t experience any sound problems, there were several quality of life things that sealed the dislike for the Lifeproof FRE case.

PRO:
—The built-in screen protector is pretty good. I liked that I didn’t have to install it myself, as it’s part of the case.

CONS:
—Within minutes of putting the Lifeproof FRE case on her phone, I dropped it. The back of the case is slick, some kind of hard plastic instead of the grippier TPU case. The Lifeproof case just didn’t feel nice to hold in my hand, and with the slicker plastic, I worried that my mom would drop her phone as well.

—The little “door” that protects the charger port was super hard for her to open. Every time my mom wanted to charge her phone, I had to come do it for her, since she couldn’t get the door open. I understand needing a tight seal for the waterproof protection, but there has to be an easier way to access the charger port.

—The small oval cut out for charging cords was too small for my non Apple Lightning cables. I have two that are Apple certified, AmazonBasics and Zerolemon, and neither fit.

—My mom found it impossible to manipulate any of the buttons. I assume the buttons will loosen up over months, but boy, they are super hard to press when the case is new.

My mom’s not quite the intended audience for the case, but as she plans to keep her iPhone for a few years, we want it to stay in nice shape. And you never know when you’re going to drop your phone into a snowbank or puddle, so having a waterproof case adds peace of mind. But I’ll have to keep looking for her, because the Lifeproof FRE had a couple of little problems that added up to big annoyances.
text_fidelity_b: Lifeproof FRĒ SERIES iPhone 6/6s Waterproof Case (4.7" Version) - Retail Packaging - SUNSET (PIPELINE/WINDSURF/LONGBOARD)

TP-Link EAP115 V4 | Omada N300 Ceiling Mount Wireless Access Point | PoE Powered | Easy Installation | SDN Integrated | Cloud Access & Omada app for Easy Management | White I recently dumped my consumer grade mesh network for a home built pfsense router and added these AP's along with the OC200 for management. I have to say that the firmware upgraded has provided a fantastic experience mgt of wifi. Guest configuration including setting up basic captive portal and VLAN is easy. Signal in my home has never been better. I have 3 AP's covering 3 floors without issue. Stability seems rock solid so far.

Will continue to update as time goes on..

9/8/2020
Still enjoying this product combined with their oc200 and my pfsense NUC. The OC200 makes mgt of your WiFi a breeze. Stability is fantastic and speeds are still rock solid. Roof mounting APs still beats mesh satellites sitting in various rooms. Setting up vlan and configuring a captive portal guest wifi were easy. I would still like to have some additional reporting and block functions related URLs at some level. Btw..the people complaining about the inability to get 300 Mg down close range. I get 350 pinned. I'm approximately 10 ft right now from one of my ap's. My suggestion to them is maybe look at a better router or better internet provider....

9/14/2020
After upgrading my Router, tweaking and confirming my new 1GB service speed, I am not happy with results and lowering my review pending an update from TPLINK support. I should be getting closer to gig down with CAT 6e cable and a GS108PEv3 (Powered switch) Best I can get is 400 mb right below the AP. More to come...

20/27/2020
Can't find where my network is being throttled. Short of adding an access point from a competitor, I should clearly be exceeding 300 mb. The POE switch is a GS108PEv3, I have router with 1 gb ports (physical connection gets close to 1gb) and cat 6e cable throughout. I have to assume it's something to do with the AP's. Tech support has sucked for lack of better words. (thanks for the canned FAQ that was useless..) Stability is great..but need this solved..

Sept 2021
After several updates, further tuning, I am pleased with stability of the wifi and speeds. I am getting slightly better speeds. The key is stability. I don't have drops like my original consumer neteork equipment that I had in the past.

Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender The tech geek in our household kept telling me there was nothing we could do to improve on the truly horrendous wireless internet service we have. He said we were stuck with the ISP we have and with their router (which he has in the far back bedroom, on the other side of our apartment from the pricey smart TV I haven't been able to use for anything but watching cable news). I haven't been able to stream anything from Amazon Prime, nor can I access the internet at all through the TV. So in complete frustration, without telling him, I ordered the Securifi Almond. Price was one factor in my decision, but I knew I wasn't going to be able to depend on him to help me set anything up and I'm not all that tech savvy.

One of the attractive selling points of this router is that it can be used either as a router or as a range extender. I planned to set it up as a range extender to see if I could get a better signal near my TV, but also had in mind that I might be able to persuade a certain somebody to try it as our router in place of the one that I feel like is defective (or just crummy) from our ISP.

I set it up myself. I just followed the installation on screen, and it was a snap. Fortunately, I knew what our log-in info was for our network so I didn't have to ask for help. I wasn't sure how it was supposed to work with the ethernet cable, so I plugged the Almond into the LAN port of of my TV and into one of the ports with a TV icon on the router. Then I tested it. Wow. The streaming is so much better than it was that I signed up for Netflix and started binging on "House of Cards." I still have the rotating download timer come up once or twice during an episode, but it gets done pretty quickly and the episode finishes playing. Before, I couldn't even load an episode or, worse, it would play a minute then completely drop the connection to the internet.

So I'm quite happy. This is a sleek little baby that works. I can see at a glance that I'm connected, which is reassuring. I haven't yet tried it in its router mode, but as a range extender it works great. You need to use the little stowaway stylus that comes with it when you're selecting onscreen functions, but as long as you remember to re-stow it, you've always got it handy if you need it.
text_fidelity_b: Securifi Almond - (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Wireless Router/Range Extender

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear TL;DR— not worth the extra cost, it will break and the lifetime warranty is a scam (website doesn’t work, always out of stock), just order a cheaper one and replace— IF you can somehow get Zagg to honor the warranty they will charge you at least $7 to send you a new one when this breaks (and it will def. break)

This was a great screen protector for the several months it lasted before cracking. That partially justifies the steep price tag compared to other screen protectors— but not really.

After I purchased this from amazon I registered this product on the Zagg website, which is necessary to potentially claim a replacement through the “lifetime” warranty program. When it broke, I logged back into their website to order a replacement. The first thing that was annoying was they had a message saying any product ordered within a several years long period would need to be re-registered after they had redesigned their website— my screen protector did not fall into this category, but I assume many people were out of luck on their warranties since they probably no longer had their receipts from screen protectors they had already registered. There was no email or anything warning consumers of this issue, although it’s possible it went out to only the affected people.

When I tried to order a replacement for my broken screen protector I got an error message telling me to try again later. Then the screen protector was out of stock. Then the website is down for maintenance. Then it was out of stock again. The Zagg screen protector on my phone is also broken and also had a warranty. Between the two I have been unable to order a replacement despite trying many, many times. I‘m not a computer engineer or anything, but my computer literacy is usually sufficient to navigate consumer websites. I’m pretty sure the issue is not with me, and if I am doing something wrong it’s because they have intentionally made their website impossible to navigate.

Eventually I gave up and just replaced the screen protector on my phone with a cheaper one. I was able to buy 2 new screen protectors for the same price as the SHIPPING for what the warranty replacement for the Zagg screen protector would have been if it was ever in stock when their website was working, and the difference in quality is negligible.

I don’t appreciate paying extra for a warranty that is not honored and having my time wasted trying to order a replacement when it’s clearly designed to be impossible. I also ended up keeping a broken screen protector on my phone and iPad for months while trying over and over again to order my replacement since it was under warranty.
text_fidelity_b: ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I loved how simple it was to get this set up and working. I just followed the instructions and it connected to my home wireless network without a hiccup. The image quality is OK. Decent for a basic webcam. Good enough for my purposes.

GOOD:
Simple to set up and get working.
Quality is adequate
Cheap!
Multiple cameras work well. Just different tabs for different cameras on the web view.
iPhone App: Great! Also very easy to use. Watching your camera(s) on the iPhone is actually easier a less glitchy than watching on the PC.

BAD:
Pretty short range for the wireless. I get better wireless range with my laptop and iPhone (802.11N). I actually bought a range extender so I could connect a 2nd DCS-930L camera just 40 ft away (but through two walls).
Short power cord
Web Viewers are not so great. The remote web viewer (MyDlink) has resolution issues and Java issues. Works but you have to click an extra OK or two. And the viewer takes a few seconds to load. The "local" web view - directly through your own network - also has Java issues - prompting you to authorize the app every time you load it (it doesn't remember the authorization - at least not on my computer which is updated with the latest Java as of 6-8-13). They should really work on this. Also, it'd be nice if the viewer were more stripped down so you don't have to have a big window open. Just The Video Please.

Not only would I buy this again, but I'd buy a 2nd one. I've tried to configure other wireless cameras through the firewall, forwarding ports blah blah blah. Sometimes it works. Sometimes not. This one just works. And it has the nifty smartphone apps. In my book, for the price, that gets it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Fitbit Charge Wireless Activity Wristband, Black, Small Sooooo, I bought this Fitbit for myself randomly. I was so excited to receive it and it looked very sleek and nice! I wore it just about everywhere. Three weeks into having it, I traveled to New Orleans with the Fitbit on my wrist... I arrived at the hotel late in the evening and realized something felt different. So I checked my pockets, and looked around the floor of my hotel room, when I finally realized what it was. My Fitbit was gone! No where in sight. Not anywhere on the floor, no where. I had no idea it was missing, and I was so sad. I had no idea where it was, so it literally popped off my wrist somewhere at the airport or in the taxi, and I didn't even realize it until it was too late. I even bought an App on my iPhone to help me try and find my Fitbit, but that didn't work at all and it was a waste of $4.99. I don't have $89 to spare to buy a brand new one, which also sucks.

It's a great product, but I personally recommend spending the extra $30 for the Fitbit Charge HR because it is like a watch wrist band, rather than just a snap on one, so you don't ever have to worry about it just popping off! If I ever got a new one, I would most likely buy the Fitbit Charge HR.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge Wireless Activity Wristband, Black, Small

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Zen Sleek Photo 20 GB Multimedia Player (Aluminum/White) I was in the market for a hard drive-based music player and didn't want to go the normal iPxx route, so I began checking into different brands. I had a list of criteria that the player had to meet:

-EXCELLENT SOUND. This is critical. A SnR (Signal to Noise Ratio) of 95db or better

-Excellent battery life. At least 15 hours

-At least 20 GB

-A color screen

-Sturdy build

-As little touch-sensitive controlling as possible. Click wheels are inaccurate and bothersome.

-Ease of use. Drag and drop is preferred.

-AC adapter for charging on the road or from an AC converter in a car

This player meets all of those needs. The SnR is 97db, I've gotten 18 hours out of the battery (remember that increased settings like equalizers and higher bitrates mean lower battery life for ALL players), the case is solid and brushed aluminum, the screen is pretty and quite sharp, only one touch-sensitive control is present, the player CAN drag and drop through Win XP, and it comes with a wall adapter.

I love the powerful sound this puts out and it can drive my big headphones with no problem. It can, like most HDD players, set aside a partition for storage. It has a good FM tuner, recording of FM and a little mic for voice notes. It can even sync with Outlook for contacts and other info. The hard disk seems fast and

Now for the drawbacks:

-You can't watch 15fps video on a tiny screen and reduce your battery life by 67%

-The USB cable is proprietary...no mini USB!

-The wall charger cable plugs into the USB cable...this means two cables for recharging from the wall

-Looking at photos and playing music at the same time is not possible

-Creative software is always iffy. Thankfully, in Win XP, you can open the player from My Computer and access its contents directly with non-DRM music and photos.

-Battery is NON-USER REPLACEABLE. This is odd for Creative.

-No mention of this on the Creative website. Thankfully, updated drivers ARE available from support.

This player would have been state-of-the-art about a year ago, but has been eclipsed by its bigger brother the Zen Vision with 30 and 60GB drives and video...however, if you're not buying into the "kill your eyes with tiny video on tiny screens" and just want a SOLID and RELIABLE player with booming sound, this is it!!! You can tell it's custom-made for Windows (it's MTP, not UMS for any computer), but if you're running XP, then it's a solid choice because you can skip the Creative software and just load music on it.

If you can get it on sale like I did, snatch it up. This is a little gem of a player!
text_fidelity_b: Creative Zen Sleek Photo 20 GB Multimedia Player (Aluminum/White)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show - 1st Generation Black If there were a way to give this negative stars I'd do it. Amazon, seriously. I don't understand you guys. Half the time you do great things and the other half the time I frankly at am a loss for words. Do you do ANY testing at all before you go to market? Seriously, who decided this was ready to be sold as is.

Me: Alexa show my videos
Echo: Here are your photos.

Me: Alexa show me my movies.
Echo: here are your videos. ( I asked for videos and got photos. I have for movies and it gives me my videos. )
but then it only shows me about 20 of my more than 100 movie Library.

Me: Alexa, show me a calendar
Echo: here is what's on the calendar. (no, I want to see a calendar month for this month)
I tried everything. There is no calendar. If I wanted to see events, I'd ask to see events. See how that is logical? I want to see a calendar. It's not rocket science. It's that basic thing that hangs on everyone's wall? You know a 30 day calendar?

So I begin to think maybe this isn't my account...

Me: Alexa, who's account is this.
Echo: This device has only one account, Alex's.
A last name would be good here. Lot's of Alex's out there.

Me: Alex's show me what's on prime video
Echo: YouTube plays something I have no idea what it is.

I can't ask what's on prime video. It has no concept of what I am asking. And this just goes on and on. Stick with me Amazon. I have an idea. You have a video based Echo. Maybe, just maybe, it would be a good idea that we could ask this video based echo what new movies are on prime video?? Yah think? I eventually got it to show me some prime movies. It seems to pick 20 to show as a selection. Kind of like when it showed me a selection of 20 of my movie library even though I have well over a hundred.

Me: Alexa, show songs from my library.
Echo: this shows 50 random songs from my library.

Me: Alexa, show albums in my library.
Echo: this shows 50 albums. Better than the response I got from my movies query.

Here are some request to make this living disaster better.

Me: Alexa, show me my video collection.
This should result in showing me movies and tv shows I own and/or have rented. I should be able to choose movies from here.
once in movies, I should be able to search for a movie by name from this point.

Me: Alexa, show me a calendar.
This should result in showing me a calendar for the current month, with Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun across the top and all the numbers of the weeks below. I ought to be able to then say, what's going on for the 14th. And it should be the 14th. I should be able to say, add event for the 14th and then add the event. I know, rocket science, right?

Me: Alexa, show me holidays for this month.
The result, I think you know...

If I ask to see my shopping list it says I have one item "1 Song" if I ask it to show me 1 or song or both it fails to understand what I am talking about.

Bottom line, this is JUST NOT FINISHED. Not by a country mile. You have to be kidding me if you think this is ready for the end user.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show - 1st Generation Black

Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black Boy is this big. Fortunately it fits just barely in my Sentey Gaming case. I had purchased the Arctic Freezer 7 Pro Rev 2 but that was far worse than the AMD 8350's included cooler fan, probably because the contact surface is designed for Intel chips and is much smaller than for AMD chips.
Be prepared for some work installing this fan as you have to install a new back-plate on the motherboard. The included parts are perfect in that they provide everything you will need including the thermal compound. So I also purchased the 2 top case fans (Corsair series). Without the cooler, the top fans did indeed reduce the top CPU temperatures by about 4C degrees - almost as though the case cover is open. With the cooler though the CPU temperature never climbed beyond 61C degrees even when all 8 cores were saturated (was compiling code). Without the cooler and the the top fans I was hitting 70C degrees which is 5 degrees above allowed operating temperature. I am surprised my AMD 8350 is still operational. With the cooler and top fans the temperature drop is 15C which is a win! Maybe I can use the Arcrtic Freezer in an Intel setup.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

text_fidelity_a:
Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White This is an extremely comfortable to wear set of lightweight over-ear headphones.

There's often a lot of noise in my house. A television on somewhere, dishes being done, and a nine year old that never stops talking. I like to use headphones as an escape. When headphones claim they are noise isolating I hold them to it. These headphones did not disappoint me. The nicely cushioned soft pleather covered ear cups adjust for angle to offer a secure fit that provides excellent insulation against ambient noise and are very comfortable to wear, even for extended periods of time.

I found that they could deliver the snap of live instruments, or the impression that I was at a club with the singer on the stage in front of me. When the music had stopped, there was still silence. I noticed that I enjoyed wearing them because of the peace and quiet, I didn't want to take them off actually. These headphones isolate out noise so well they made me consider wearing them when the kid's home just to be able to hear myself think.

The sound quality is crisp, great clarity not overpowering and provide a personal ambience. They offer a great balance and at no point was I confused when watching movies. They were even picking up the weighty and seismic bass from Jurassic Park that would imply a dinosaur was right behind me. The adjustable aluminum headphone band has a slight amount of padding beneath the pleather covered top part, but I wish it had just a little bit more to provide a bit more cushioning. Finally, the headphones are able to smoothly swivel flat for storage or packing although the cable is too long for me to want to use these for trips.

Overall I am incredibly happy with their quality, especially for the price. They're very comfortable, provide excellent noise isolation, and deliver very clean response with deep bass. I plan to enjoy using them and am pleased to recommend them on Amazon.

Retail sample provided at no cost by Edifier for my testing, evaluation, and review.
text_fidelity_b: Edifier P841 Comfortable Noise Isolating Over-Ear Headphones with Microphone and Volume Controls - White

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black First of all, I'm looking at reviews and pictures of other peoples item and it seems they have a different item, and yet all the reviews are together. Let me start with the good...

PROS_ Inexpensive!

Cons_

THE INSTRUCTIONS: they are written in 6 different languages, and it jumps back and forth between them. It's not broken English, but very hard to follow. Some of them even have a sort of thumbnail of an entire page of text compressed into about 1.5." It is very bizarre. It took about 30 minutes of studying the pictures to figure out what the heck to do, because the manual certainly doesn't tell you. The box comes with sooo much extra hardware to account for different sizes and mounting situations, but the manual does not explain this well.

THE HARDWARE: It is super heavy duty and weighs nearly as much as my TV. My TV is super light weight and is probably 8 or 9 lbs. The bolts that screw into the stud could hold 100lbs I'm sure. Even pre-drilling pilot holes I had difficulty screwing them in with a drill they are so big. It takes so much torque that the screws stripped. I ended up using 1.5" wood screws. I used a stud and I don't like where the TV is mounted, so I am going to get molly bolts to screw it into the drywall where I would like to put it.

NOT STURDY: You mount a plate to the back of the TV, then you mount another piece of hardware to the wall. You then attach the TV to the hardware you just attached to the wall. It is wobbly. It also tilts anywhere from a perfectly neutral position to 20 degree or so angle down. This is in case you are mounting it very high and wish to tilt it down. The TV keeps flopping forward and tilting down. There is a bolt that keeps it in place and I tightened the heck out of it, and it just barely stays put.

NOT FLUSH: I have no other mounting systems to compare it to, but the TV sticks out about 2.5" from the wall. I was expecting it to be much closer.

So there you have it. I am not happy. Ultimately I have the mounted now and no real reason to return it because it's doing what I need it to. There are a lot of positive reviews, but they are I'm sure for a different product. Anyways I paid $15.95. You will most likely be happier with something you pay $25 for.

I included photos of the manual. You can see how the TV mounts, all the extra hardware, as well as a few pages of horrible manual- complete with the mini thumbnail pages.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Kindle 9W PowerFast Adapter for Accelerated Charging I purchased this to go along with my new 8.9 inch Fire HD (and I'm counting the days until it arrives), but it also works with the original Fire. I found the major benefit for the original Fire to be the better form factor -- unlike the "wart" shape of the original Fire charger, this is much more sleek, with folding plugs to make it very easy to carry in a case. Very simple, clean design.

The downside to using it with the original Fire is that you need to provide your own cable from the charger to the Fire, as the charger does NOT include it.

The charge time is only slightly faster for the original Fire. Using the app Battery HD to measure charge time and level, the new charger saved about 15 minutes to go from a 15% charge to a 100% charge versus the original charger. Faster, but not a huge gain. I expect that the differential in terms of charge time for the new Fire (especially the 8.9 inch one) will be much greater when comparing this charger with using a USB port to charge. I'll post results once I have my 8.9 inch Fire.

While it's not a compelling purchase if you have the original Fire, it is worth getting (at 50% off) if ordered with a new HD Fire, especially if you can also get the MP3 credit. I'm giving it 5-stars since, at the price paid, it's very handy to have as a spare charger, and it's MUCH easier to take along than the original Fire charger.

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors) This jumpdrive is USB 3.0 (fast) but backward compatible with 2.0. It's a little cheesy looking because of its plastic "bubblegum" look, but the color-coding of the different size drives could be useful. I got the bright green 32 GB USB 3.0 stick for review, and when I put it into my USB port it showed installation files on the drive for both Windows and Mac. I double-clicked the Mac for my MacBook Pro, and it presented me with the installation screens. It was a little confusing how to get the software installed, and initially I had to install it on my computer to access the installation for just the flash drive; it's supposed to be optional to install it on your computer, but it wasn't apparent how to bypass computer installation. I had to delete my computer vault after it was created to get it off my computer.

Another confusion is that you are taken to a website with an offer for an Encryptstick software upgrade for a reduced cost or free for a 14-day trial. Apparently, all the best features of this device are not available if you just use the stick as a USB drive with the standard "Encryptstick Lite" app that comes with it. You will have AES encryption, but not the "military grade encryption," whatever that means. (The website lists the option to encrypt vaults with 128, 256, or 512-bit AES ciphers [1024-bit coming], registered and government approved, FIPS 140-2 compliant). Here are the other features listed on the website and, again, it's not clear which come with the standard installation and which with the upgraded one:

Runs on Multiple OS computers and all recently made USB flash drives
Encrypt & Decrypt Your Private Files
Easy to Use Encryption Interface [debatable!]
Speedy Auto-Updater
Lost Flash Drive Data Recovery Feature
Advanced Virtual Keyboard
Lock out Computer Installation is Optional - Not Essential
Lock out No Admin Rights Required
File Wipe Instant Lock
Quick Search, Live Search
Automatic Timeout
Limited Login Attempts
File Wipe File Shredder

I went on and purchased the upgrade (12.99 to Lexar users instead of the usual 39.99) because the advanced backup features are only available with the upgraded version and I did want them, but I thought it was a little sneaky how they presented all this. It's really not clear that you don't have to get the upgrade to make the stick itself work. Once you've purchased the upgrade, you are given links to download the upgrade for all versions (PC, Mac, and Linux) in an email.

Somehow I wound up with both the EncryptStick Lite and EncryptStick apps both running at the same time. I could not close out of either one of them, and attempting to eject the jumpdrive gave me an error saying I needed to close out of both apps. I had to force-quit the Lite app. That made me nervous about the whole thing.

I have to mention the following experience because, for me, it was an issue. The little lanyard (about the length of the drive when installed) is not attached when you take it out of the package, and I had a heck of a time getting it threaded through the end. The cord won't bend through the jumpdrive's hole, so it requires using an implement of some come to grasp the thread end and pull it through. My tweezers were too large, and so was the end of the large paperclip (all I had), so I wound up having to strip off the coating on an old bobby pin that I just happened to have lying in a drawer. Even then, I had to pop up part of the plastic cover on the front of the drive case a little to work the thread through, and I was worried about destroying the drive in the process. This whole process was very aggravating, so I think it would be better if they sold these with the lanyard already attached. Customers can then remove it if they don't want it, but I think the lanyard is quite useful. If you have more than one of these drives, you could hang them all up on a keyholder at your desk, then pull one off to take with you as needed.

Please note that I am downrating this product because of the initial confusion and hassles above, although in fairness this is not a good indication of the reliability and performance of the jumpdrive once the software and lanyard are installed. Consider this review to be of the initial experience with the jumpdrive and software. If I discover any more problems as I use this drive over time, I will come back and post them. For now, though, I'm tired of fooling with it!
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors)

text_fidelity_a:

This replaces an old KEF center speaker and the difference can be clearly heard. The Polk has a crisp, clean sound that clarifies and enhances dialog but not at the expense of a nice solid bass (although I also have a subwoofer in the setup).

Aesthetically it's a simple, clean design. Normally I don't pay much attention to the look of a speaker but in this case, since it's a center speaker, it's in my line of sight all the time. It's about as unobtrusive you can get with a center speaker without compromising sound quality and performance. Polk did an excellent job with the design.

I looked at the new version of this (the ES35) and, while there are some small incremental improvements, I didn't consider them to be worth the extra $100 it costs. Plus, this was on a price dip for the differential between the two was $150, making this the clear choice.

While I have been partial to KEF in the past for speakers, the performance of this Polk has really wow'd me. At present I'm using this center speaker with KEF left and right front speakers, and KEF for surround. I've been so impressed with the ES35 that I'll be changing to Polk for my L/R soon, and keep the KEF only for surround (5.1.2 setup).

An excellent center speaker that hits the mark on all counts. Five stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.
text_fidelity_b: Cyber Acoustics Stereo USB Headset (AC-5008A), in-line Controls for Volume & Mic Mute, Adjustable Mic Boom for PC & Mac, Perfect for Classroom or Home

text_fidelity_a:
Vanguard TBH-100 Ball Head (Black) When I purchased my Dolica AX620B100 tripod, it was advertised as having a ball head. However, the ball head on that tripod only moves side to side, it doesn't fully rotate. Since most of my photography is outdoors in the landscape, it took a little doing to make sure my photographs were level even on bumpy ground.

This Vanguard ball head attachment fixes all of that. I have three tripods and one monopod in the house, and it attached easily to all of them. The ball head is easy to adjust and has an intuitive friction control lever which allows you to move the ball head just a little or a lot. I feel like I've got great control. However, it never gets fully floppy to where you could accidentally damage your camera, as with a ball head I tried in the store.

I also really liked the turning action of the quick release knob, it feels a lot more secure than the usual lever that I'm used to.

Overall, this is a great addition to my humble set of landscape photography and video equipment. It's easy to use, took me about two minutes to figure out and attach, and gives me much better functionality than I had previously.

text_fidelity_a: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc… I’ve had this for 8 months with no issues, then I got an under-the-desk treadmill and the screens go black and immediately come back on ALL THE TIME. I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.
text_fidelity_b: Selore&S-Global USB C to Dual HDMI Adapter 4K @60hz, Type C to HDMI Converter for MacBook Pro Air 2020/2019/2018,LenovoYoga 920/Thinkpad T480,Dell XPS 13/15,etc…

Jabra Stealth Bluetooth Headset - Black (US Version) I am pleased with this headset; the sound quality is good and audibility is very sharp. The music quality is also good. Assembly is very simple and needs no additional tools to set it together. It also fits well into my ears. I have been using this set for the last three weeks and it works great. It is paired with my cell phone and I use this to listen to the incoming calls and also listen to the music from micro SD card inserted into the cell phone. It is small and has a discreet design. It is very light, easy to carry and works great. The gadget also synchronizes easily with phone, but it does not pair with my Garmin Nuvi GPS machine or my Acer Chromebook both of which are Bluetooth-enabled.

Pairing with cell phone is very easy; just turn the headset on and the cell phone on, it detects the Bluetooth easily and within a minute it gives the message that it is paired. The built-in battery is excellent, and on one charge it lasts for about 5-6 hours of use time. The downside is that this piece doesn't have a separate mute button or the volume button; you have to control volume from your cell phone. Another negative feature is that the three replacement parts for earpiece that comes with the set are of same size, hence gives little option for someone with small (or large) ears. I have rated this product four stars for overall satisfaction.
